official_authorities.label: NRS 17.130 — computation and interest on judgments
1987 Nevada act — current formula's cause-of-action transition
Torres v. Goodyear — Nevada Supreme Court simple-interest authority

calculation.reason: The official semiannual history, prime-plus-two formula, reset schedule, simple-interest rule, and general accrual trigger are verified, but contract, judgment-specified, other-law, consumer-form-debt, offer-of-judgment, future-damages, day-count, and payment-allocation branches are not calculator-complete.

branches.general_default: NRS 17.130(2): FID prime immediately preceding judgment plus two points, resetting each January 1 and July 1 while unpaid
branches.contract_other_law_or_judgment: A lawful contract, another law, or the judgment itself can specify a different rate
branches.consumer_form_debt: NRS 97B.150 uses the lesser qualifying contract rate or prime plus two, fixes the selected rate at judgment, bars compounding, and has exemptions
branches.future_damages: Interest on future-damages amounts begins at judgment rather than service
branches.offer_of_judgment_and_special_rules: NRS Chapter 17 contains additional offer-of-judgment and special-interest branches that are not modeled here

annual_rate.notes: Nevada FID publishes a 6.75% prime rate for July 1 through December 31, 2026, producing an 8.75% general NRS 17.130(2) judgment rate. The general rate resets each January 1 and July 1 while unpaid and accrues as simple interest. Interest ordinarily begins at service of the summons and complaint; the future-damages component begins at judgment. A lawful contract, another law, the judgment itself, or qualifying consumer-form debt can require a different path. Reference only; not legal advice.
